title: SQL Set 03: Banking Ledger, Running Totals & Self-Joins
description: Window frame running balances, net account transfers, consecutive transaction deltas via LAG, and manager hierarchies.

queries.title: Account Running Balance Over Time
queries.prompt: Calculate the cumulative `running_balance` for each `acct_id` ordered chronologically by `txn_date` and `txn_id`. Return `acct_id`, `txn_id`, `amount`, and `running_balance`, sorted by `acct_id`, `txn_date`, `txn_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE ledger (txn_id INT PRIMARY KEY, acct_id INT, txn_date TEXT, amount INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT acct_id, txn_id, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY acct_id ORDER BY txn_date, txn_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_balance FROM ledger ORDER BY acct_id, txn_date, txn_id;
queries.explanation: Explicit `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` prevents tie-grouping pitfalls on identical dates.

queries.title: Employees Earning More Than Their Manager
queries.prompt: Write a self-join on `bank_staff` to find the `emp_name` of employees whose `salary` strictly exceeds their direct manager's `salary`. Order alphabetically.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE bank_staff (emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY, emp_name TEXT, salary INT, manager_id INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT e.emp_name FROM bank_staff e JOIN bank_staff m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.salary > m.salary ORDER BY e.emp_name;
queries.explanation: Self-join matches `e.manager_id = m.emp_id`; inner join naturally drops the top executive whose `manager_id` is NULL.

queries.title: Transaction Amount Change vs Previous Deposit
queries.prompt: For `CREDIT` rows only in `bank_events`, return `acct_id`, `event_id`, `amount`, and `diff_from_prev` (`amount` minus the previous `CREDIT` amount for that `acct_id`, or NULL for the first credit). Order by `acct_id`, `event_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE bank_events (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, acct_id INT, kind TEXT, amount INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT acct_id, event_id, amount, amount - LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY acct_id ORDER BY event_id) AS diff_from_prev FROM bank_events WHERE kind = 'CREDIT' ORDER BY acct_id, event_id;
queries.explanation: `WHERE kind = 'CREDIT'` runs before window functions (`LAG`), ensuring `DEBIT` events are skipped cleanly.

queries.title: Net Peer-to-Peer Transfer Balance
queries.prompt: Compute net balance change per account across all transfers in `transfers` (`to_acct` gains `amt`, `from_acct` loses `amt`). Return `acct_no` and `net_change`, ordered by `net_change` descending, `acct_no` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE transfers (tx_id INT PRIMARY KEY, from_acct INT, to_acct INT, amt INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT acct_no, SUM(delta) AS net_change FROM (SELECT to_acct AS acct_no, amt AS delta FROM transfers UNION ALL SELECT from_acct AS acct_no, -amt AS delta FROM transfers) t GROUP BY acct_no ORDER BY net_change DESC, acct_no ASC;
queries.explanation: `UNION ALL` splits each double-entry transfer into one credit row and one debit row before summing by `acct_no`.

queries.title: Accounts Using Multiple Payment Channels
queries.prompt: Find `acct_id` values in `channel_logs` that performed transactions across at least 3 distinct channels, ordered by `acct_id` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE channel_logs (log_id INT PRIMARY KEY, acct_id INT, channel TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT acct_id FROM channel_logs GROUP BY acct_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT channel) >= 3 ORDER BY acct_id;
queries.explanation: `COUNT(DISTINCT channel)` prevents repeated uses of `'UPI'` from inflating the channel count.
